name: Semantic search over a column
desc: Embed a text column once with Titan, then rank rows by meaning for any query

cells.code:
## 🔎 Semantic search over a column

Find rows by **meaning**, not keywords. A keyword filter misses "the checkout kept spinning" when you search "payment failed"; a semantic search ranks it near the top because the *embeddings* are close. The trick to doing this cheaply: **embed the corpus once** with Amazon Titan v2, keep the vectors, and reuse them for every query — re-embedding the whole column on each search is the slow, costly mistake this recipe avoids.

**Flow:** load a text column → `embed_texts` the corpus once → `semantic_search(query, corpus, corpus_vectors=...)` for any number of queries. The embedding round-trip is install-free and uses the VM's execution role — no keys, no `pip install`.

# 1) Load rows that have a free-text column to search over (reviews, tickets,
#    descriptions, ...). Swap the reader for whatever holds your text.
df = read_athena("SELECT * FROM <table_with_text> LIMIT 1000")
df.head()

# 2) Embed the corpus ONCE with Titan v2. Keep corpus_vectors around — this is the
#    expensive step and you never want to repeat it per query.
corpus = df["<text_column>"].tolist()
corpus_vectors = embed_texts(corpus)
print("embedded", corpus_vectors.shape[0], "rows into", corpus_vectors.shape[1], "dims")

# 3) Query. Passing corpus_vectors makes this a pure vector comparison — it does NOT
#    re-embed the corpus, only the short query. Returns a DataFrame (rank, score, text)
#    sorted by similarity. Run this cell as many times as you like with new queries.
hits = semantic_search("<your query>", corpus, corpus_vectors=corpus_vectors, top_k=5)
hits

# 4) Join the matches back to the original rows for full context (ids, dates,
#    revenue, ...). semantic_search returns the matched `text` + `score`; merge on the
#    text column to recover every other field of the winning rows.
top = hits.merge(df, left_on="text", right_on="<text_column>", how="left")
top.head()
